paper.title: Pure Exploration for Constrained Best Mixed Arm Identification with a Fixed Budget

settings.name_in_paper: Constrained best mixed arm identification (CBMAI) with a fixed budget
unmapped: Each arm yields a Gaussian reward and L Gaussian costs; goal is to identify the support of the best mixed arm (distribution over arms) maximizing expected reward subject to L expected-cost constraints c p <= c_bar
First K_0 arms have unknown means; remaining K-K_0 arms have known reward/cost means, given to the algorithm
Strict criterion: output support must equal exactly the optimal basis (including slack variables)
Assumption 1: the LP has a unique optimal solution with exactly L+1 non-zero coordinates (non-degenerate)
Variances need not be known by the algorithm but are assumed known for analysis
settings.definition_quote: We would like to determine a mixed arm $p^*$, i.e., a probability distribution over the arms ... such that it achieves $\max_{p\in \distset_K}\{\mathbf{R}^T p : \mathbf{C} p \leq \costbound \}$ ... We consider a fixed-budget setting, i.e., we can only obtain at most $N$ such samples ... minimizes the misidentification probability $\Pr_{\mathbf{r},\mathbf{c}}(\armset^{\mathrm{\phi}} \neq \mathcal{I}^*)$

settings.name_in_paper: CBMAI with a fixed budget, Gaussian instances with known variances, all arms unknown (lower bound)
unmapped: Each arm yields Gaussian reward and L Gaussian costs with fixed known variances; identify support of best mixed arm under L expected-cost constraints
Instance class: infeasible instances or instances satisfying Assumption 1 (unique non-degenerate LP optimum)
settings.definition_quote: We consider a class of instances with Gaussian rewards and costs such that the variances $\sigma_c^2, \sigma_r^2$ are fixed and known ... For simplicity, we consider $K_0 = K$, i.e., all arms are unknown.

algorithms.name: Score Function-based Successive Reject (SFSR) with intersection value score

symbols.L_c: number of cost constraints L (treated as constant in O_L)
symbols.N_tilde: (T - K_0)/(3*((L_c+1)/2 + log(K_0))), with T the budget N
symbols.K_0: number of arms with unknown means
symbols.Delta_0: optimal support infeasibility gap (Gaussian-normalized distance to making the optimal basis infeasible)
symbols.H_gap: min_{2<=i<=K} Delta_{(i+L)}^2 / i, where Delta_{(k)} is the k-th smallest arm value gap

conditions: Assumption 1: LP has a unique optimal solution with exactly L+1 non-zero coordinates
Gaussian rewards N(r_a, sigma_r^2) and costs N(c_{l,a}, sigma_c^2), mutually independent
tuning: T_k as in eq. (Tk) with Psi(K_0,L)

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Let $\armset^{\fcnm}$ denote the output of Algorithm \ref{algo:ivsr}. Then, under Assumption \ref{assump:unique}, we have $\Pr(\armset^{\fcnm} \neq \mathcal{I}^* ) \leq \bigO_L(K)\cdot \exp(-\Tilde{N} \Delta_0^{2}/K) + \bigO_L(K^{L+2}) \cdot\exp(-\min_{2\leq i\leq K}\Tilde{N}\Delta_{(i+L)}^2 /i)$ where $\Tilde{N} := \frac{N - K_0}{3(\frac{L+1}{2} + \log K_0)}$ and $\bigO_L$ is the standard big-O notation where $L$ is treated as a constant.

results.notes: Budget N mapped to T. O is with respect to K with L treated as constant. Proof gives explicit constants (K-1)3^{L(L+1)/2} and K(K+1)/2 binom(K+L-1,L) 3^{(L+1)^2}. Paper also derives the exponent liminf -1/N log P >= min{Delta_0^2/K, Delta_(L+2)^2/2, ..., Delta_(L+K)^2/K}/(3((L+1)/2+log K)) as a consequence. Probability field set to 'expectation' since the quantity is itself a probability.

symbols.Delta_L2: Delta_{(L+2)}, the smallest positive arm value gap

conditions: Gaussian rewards and costs with fixed known variances

source.label: prop:lowerbound
source.quote: For any consistent algorithm $\phi_N$, under any instance $\theta$ satisfying Assumption \ref{assump:unique}, the mis-identification probability satisfies $\limsup_{N\rightarrow\infty} -\dfrac{1}{N} \log\Pr_{\theta}(\mathcal{X}^{\phi_N} \neq \mathcal{I}^{\theta}) \leq \dfrac{1}{2}\min\{\Delta_0^2, \Delta_{(L+2)}^2\}.$

results.notes: Bound is on the error exponent (limsup of -(1/N) log error probability), i.e., error probability is at least roughly exp(-N * expression). Consistency in the sense of Barrier et al. 2023.

symbols.Delta_L2: Delta_{(L+2)}, the smallest positive arm value gap

conditions: Applies only to the USLP algorithm (uniform sampling then solving the empirical LP)

source.label: prop:lowerbound
source.quote: Furthermore, for the \texttt{USLP} algorithm, we have $\limsup_{N\rightarrow\infty} -\dfrac{1}{N} \log\Pr_{\theta}(\mathcal{X}^{\mathrm{USLP}_N} \neq \mathcal{I}^{\theta}) \leq \dfrac{1}{2K}\min\{\Delta_0^2, \Delta_{(L+2)}^2\}$

results.notes: Limits the error exponent of the USLP baseline (an error-probability lower bound for that specific algorithm).
